samasa.vigraha: tasya vikṣepasya pratiṣedhasya arthaḥ; acc. artham = vikṣepapratiṣedhāya

analysis.note: Adverbial accusative in -artham, ‘for the sake/purpose of’; the initial pronoun-stem tad surfaces as tat before p within the compound. Vyāsa glosses the referent as vikṣepa.

verification.detail: compound stem tatpratiṣedhārtha as Pum/Dvitiya/Eka: pass; relation tatpurusa: unsupported (logged)

samasa.vigraha: ekasya tattvasya abhyāsaḥ; bhāṣye: ekatattvāvalambanaṃ cittam abhyaset

analysis.note: Overall a tatpuruṣa, ‘practice/cultivation of a single tattva’; the subcompound eka-tattva is internally karmadhāraya, ‘a single tattva.’ Vyāsa construes this as cultivating the mind with one tattva as its support.

verification.detail: compound stem ekatattvābhyāsa as Pum/Prathama/Eka: pass; relation tatpurusa: unsupported (logged)

options_considered: prevention of the immediately preceding distraction/disturbance (vikṣepa)
prohibition or denial of ‘that’ as a proposition
prevention of every preceding item without the bhāṣya’s narrowing gloss
justifications.chosen: tat in tatpratiṣedha refers to vikṣepa, and pratiṣedha is prevention/warding-off rather than logical denial or mere prohibition.

evidence.translation: For the prevention of distraction, one should cultivate the mind resting on a single tattva.

options_considered: adverbial accusative of purpose, ‘for the sake of ...’
predicate adjective, ‘having that prevention as its aim’
an indeclinable whose relation to the practice is left unspecified
justifications.chosen: tatpratiṣedhārtham is an adverbial purpose accusative: ‘for the sake of preventing that [distraction].’

evidence.translation: For the prevention of distraction, one should cultivate the mind resting on a single tattva.

options_considered: the metaphysical One or one ultimate Reality
a single tattva/object as meditative support
the mere fact that each cognition has only one object
justifications.chosen: eka-tattva means a single principle/object serving as the mind’s support, not ‘the One Reality’ as a monistic doctrine.

evidence.translation: One should cultivate the mind resting on a single tattva for the prevention of distraction.

evidence.quote: yadi punar idaṃ sarvataḥ pratyāhṛtyaikasminn arthe samādhīyate tadā bhavaty ekāgram ity ato na pratyarthaniyatam.
evidence.translation: But if this [mind], withdrawn from all sides, is concentrated on one object, then it becomes one-pointed; therefore it is not fixed object-by-object.

options_considered: a bare abstract noun, ‘repetition/practice,’ with no prescriptive force
a prescriptive yogic cultivation of the mind
justifications.chosen: abhyāsaḥ is a practical prescription: one should cultivate/practice the citta in this one-object support.

evidence.translation: For the prevention of distraction, one should cultivate the mind resting on a single tattva.

options_considered: each momentary cognition is already ekāgra, so no special practice is needed
a stream of similar cognitions alone accounts for ekāgratā
one enduring citta is cultivated toward one-object support
justifications.chosen: The practice presupposes one enduring mind that can be distracted or made one-pointed; it is not the automatic one-pointedness of momentary object-specific cognitions or of a mere stream.

evidence.quote: yasya tu pratyarthaniyataṃ pratyayamātraṃ kṣaṇikaṃ ca cittaṃ tasya sarvam eva cittam ekāgraṃ nāsty eva vikṣiptam.
evidence.translation: For one who holds mind to be fixed to each object, mere cognition, and momentary, every mind would be one-pointed, and there would be no distracted mind at all.

evidence.quote: tasmād ekam anekārtham avasthitaṃ cittam iti.
evidence.translation: Therefore the mind is one, has many objects, and is enduring.

evidence.quote: tasmād ekam anekārtham avasthitaṃ ca cittam.
evidence.translation: Therefore the mind is one, has many objects, and is enduring.

translation: For the prevention of that [distraction, vikṣepa], there is cultivation (abhyāsa) of the mind resting on a single principle/object (eka-tattva).
one_shot_delta: A commentary-blind translation might take tat as an unspecified plural ‘those obstacles’; Vyāsa glosses the scope as vikṣepa, distraction.
It might render eka-tattva as ‘the One Reality,’ whereas the bhāṣya explains it as the mind’s support in one tattva and as concentration on one artha, a single object.
It might leave abhyāsaḥ as a bare noun ‘practice’; Vyāsa recasts it as the optative prescription cittam abhyaset, ‘one should cultivate the mind.’

It might miss the polemic against momentariness: Vyāsa insists that practice of one-pointedness belongs to a single enduring citta, not to isolated momentary cognitions that would already be ‘one-pointed.’
commentary_lines: yasya tu pratyarthaniyataṃ pratyayamātraṃ kṣaṇikaṃ ca cittaṃ tasya sarvam eva cittam ekāgraṃ nāsty eva vikṣiptam.
yadi punar idaṃ sarvataḥ pratyāhṛtyaikasminn arthe samādhīyate tadā bhavaty ekāgram ity ato na pratyarthaniyatam.
yo 'pi sadṛśapratyayapravāhena cittam ekāgraṃ manyate tasyaikāgratā yadi pravāhacittasya dharmas tadaikaṃ nāsti pravāhacittaṃ kṣaṇikatvāt.
atha pravāhāṃśasyaiva pratyayasya dharmaḥ, sa sarvaḥ sadṛśapratyayapravāhī vā visadṛśapratyayapravāhī vā pratyarthaniyatatvād ekāgra eveti vikṣiptacittānupapattiḥ.
tasmād ekam anekārtham avasthitaṃ cittam iti.
yadi ca cittenaikenānanvitāḥ svabhāvabhinnāḥ pratyayā jāyerann atha katham anyapratyayadṛṣṭasyānyaḥ smartā bhavet.
anyapratyayopacitasya ca karmāśayasyānyaḥ pratyaya upabhoktā bhavet.
kathaṃcit samādhīyamānam apy etad gomayapāyasīyanyāyam ākṣipati.
katham, yad aham adrākṣaṃ tat spṛśāmi yac cāsprākṣaṃ tat paśyāmīty aham iti pratyayaḥ sarvasya pratyayasya bhede sati pratyayiny abhedenopasthitaḥ.
ekapratyayaviṣayo 'yam abhedātmāham iti pratyayaḥ katham atyantabhinneṣu citteṣu vartamānaḥ sāmānyam ekaṃ pratyayinam āśrayet.
tasmād ekam anekārtham avasthitaṃ ca cittam.
yasya cittasyāvasthitasyedaṃ śāstreṇa parikarma nirdiśyate tat katham
